name: open, unclassified
description: A pull request exists. No itil:* class derived yet, so every rule that branches on the class has no arm to take.

name: classified
description: Exactly one itil:* class present. itil:standard/itil:normal derived by the labeller from the diff; itil:emergency only ever declared by a person.

name: class undefined
description: Two or more itil:* classes on one PR. preflight refuses (exit 2) rather than picking, because picking would mean the pipeline deciding what is an emergency. Only a person resolves it.

name: manifest asserted (labeler:skip)
description: labeler:skip is on the PR. The labeller is switched off entirely, so app:* and the class are hand-maintained. The OVERRIDE THAT TRANSFERS OWNERSHIP: no guard is silenced, the declared writer moves from labeller to human, and the PR wears the label saying so.

name: change requested
description: change:requested added by a person. The one label a human adds to set a change going; the pipeline clears it.

name: window booked
description: change:scheduled. A reservation on the path to production. An entitlement, not permission and not a promise.

name: window lapsed
description: The reservation ended unattempted and the reaper closed it. Its own closure code: not failed (nothing was attempted) and not cancelled (nobody decided against it). The change is untouched and still eligible.

name: at the moment of reliance
description: Every guard re-evaluated NOW, at activation: draft, calendar, gates, berth, estate flags, hold. This is the only place the protection layer is actually read, and it is read again on every re-entry.

name: refused: draft
description: preflight exit 6. The author's own marker says not ready. The one refusal that is the pipeline BELIEVING THE AUTHOR rather than forming a judgement. Only the author lifts it.

name: refused: behind main (guard 0)
description: mergeStateStatus BEHIND/BLOCKED/DIRTY and the divergence classifies as pipeline or worse. Bypassed by itil:emergency; the PIR then records the divergence.

name: holds the berth
description: deploy:staging. The singleton lock on the path to production, worn as a label by the PR holding it. Estate-global in effect, PR-local in form.

name: observations taken on this head
description: staging e2e / smoke / uat records exist naming THIS head SHA. Records, not labels, are what guard 4 authorizes on.

name: held by hold:staging
description: THE CONTRADICTION. hold:staging is declared REJECTED with no owner and human_add=no, and is still enforced at three sites. A person put it there; only a person may take it off; no automation may lift it and it never expires into a promotion.

name: authorized for production (guard 4)
description: Review on this head, gates green on this head, every required observation recorded on this head, no un-withdrawn failure, no hold. Authorization is about a BUILD and expires when the head moves.

name: deploying to production
description: deploy:production. Action in flight, serialized by concurrency: production with cancel-in-progress false.

name: production converged
description: production:healthy. Guard 5 sampled the estate and every sample reported the expected build. No bypass exists for this state.

name: production did not converge
description: Guard 5 refused. Rollback runs, the PIR is posted, the lock releases. itil:emergency buys nothing here.

name: evidence about a build that is no longer the head
description: The head moved, or main moved under a pass (guard 4b), or a push withdrew the observations. The measurements did not go stale: they stayed true about the build they name and stopped matching.

name: refused: someone else holds the berth
description: ESTATE-GLOBAL CAUSE. Guard 1 / preflight exit 5. One path to production, one change at a time. Recovery is wait, then rebase; the queue has no ordering, so waiting is unfair as well as slow.

name: refused: deployment lock held
description: ESTATE-GLOBAL CAUSE. blocked:lock. itil:emergency does NOT bypass this half of guard 3 -- the lock says something is physically deploying right now, which precedence cannot argue with.

name: refused: estate frozen
description: ESTATE-GLOBAL CAUSE. freeze on the estate holder (issue #1) or a stray open PR, or a scheduled FREEZE window. preflight exit 3. Blocks everyone including whoever declared it.

name: refused: frozen by nobody identifiable
description: THE STATE WITH NO NAME. The estate is shut, the record carries no actor and no reason, and the write is posted under the repo's own token. An authorised halt and a hostile one produce byte-identical records, so the recovery -- go ask the declarer -- has no addressee.

name: refused: an emergency is in flight on the estate
description: ESTATE-GLOBAL CAUSE. The bare emergency label on the estate holder. preflight exit 2. Not a class and not a precedence claim: a property of the world. Production is moving outside the normal path, so a staging pass describes a world that no longer exists.

name: refused: someone else's emergency
description: THE STATE WITH NO NAME. Another open PR carries itil:emergency -- a precedence claim about THAT change -- and it stops yours. Note the divergence: preflight's own prose says this is what it reads; its code reads the bare emergency label instead.

name: refused: by the estate flag this PR is carrying
description: THE STATE WITH NO NAME. Someone hung the bare emergency label on this PR to make the estate show an emergency handled outside the pipeline. There is deliberately NO self-exclusion, so the PR carrying the flag is blocked by it. Correct, and unnamed.

name: could not read the estate
description: THE THIRD VALUE. The calendar, the forge, the reviews endpoint, the berth query or the estate flags did not answer. preflight exit 4, which BLOCKS. Never collapses to 'no freeze' and never to 'frozen'; it is its own edge with its own recovery, which is to ask again.

name: itil:emergency declared
description: A person has declared THIS change the remedy. A precedence claim, not a readiness claim: 'if I am ready, I win over anything else'. Never inferred, never derived.

name: routed to emergency by queue pressure
description: THE ESCALATION FAILURE MODE. The berth wait exceeded patience, so the rational move is the label that skips staging. A bypass that is always available becomes the default path with extra steps; at a few hundred PRs through one berth the share tends to ~100%.

name: carrying the bypass
description: Guard 0 waived, guard 3's FREEZE half waived, guard 4 waived subject to an approving review, guard 4b waived. Guard 1 is not bypassed so much as never reached: the emergency path does not take the berth. Guard 2 and guard 5 are not waived at all.

name: holding a bypass it no longer needs
description: THE STATE WITH NO NAME. The freeze lifted, or the incident closed, and itil:emergency is still on the PR. Nothing withdraws it: the labeller does not own it and no gate may remove a person's declaration. Meanwhile it goes on outranking every other change and, per preflight's stated rule, blocking them.

name: bypass held, approval outstanding
description: The one condition attached to the guard 4 bypass: an approving review. The narrowest real check on the emergency path, and it is the check a single-identity estate cannot satisfy -- self-approval is refused by the forge.

name: refused: emergency without an approving review
description: deploy-production refuses. The bypass is conditional, and this is the condition failing. Recovery is a change authority approving, never the pipeline deciding the emergency was genuine.

name: refused: gates red, and there is no bypass
description: Guard 2 evaluated a second time on the production path precisely so the emergency route cannot skip it. An emergency may skip the staging ENVIRONMENT; it may not ship a tree whose lint and tests are red.

name: refused: production unhealthy, and there is no bypass
description: Guard 5 on the emergency path. Bypassing it would make 'deployed' a claim rather than an observation, which is the property that keeps every other bypass honest.

name: deployed, not merged, and the window is gone
description: THE STATE WITH NO NAME, named as such in the spec. Three facts at once and no vocabulary for the conjunction. Production serves a build trunk does not contain, the reservation that authorized it has closed, and the next change branches from a trunk that reverts it.

name: complete
description: change:complete. Terminal for validation and the record; never cleared. After cleanup the forge's MERGED is the record.

name: complete, record owed
description: change:complete plus change:backfill-owed. An emergency landed first and is documented after. The debt blocks nothing, survives settlement deliberately, and only a person may clear it -- automation must not clear a debt it did not pay.

name: failed
description: change:failed. Production never served this change, or never had it made live. Nothing to undo.

name: backed out
description: change:backed-out. Production DID serve this and was returned to a prior state. The word asserts an estate action, so it must name what it returned to.

name: abandoned / closed
description: Closed without merging. Not a closure code in the vocabulary, which is why an abandoned PR still holding deploy:staging wedges the berth for everyone until the reaper clears it.
